about: A rewrite of the basic Unix command-line tools (ls, cat, sort and the rest) in Rust, aiming to work the same as GNU coreutils.

prs.title: pr keeps the column separator when joining lines
prs.broken: With the option that joins full lines, pr dropped the separator between columns and between merged files, so the columns ran into each other. GNU pr keeps it.
prs.changed: pr now writes the separator in that mode like in every other mode, and a test file that had the glued output was corrected.
prs.matters: Multi-column and merged output stays readable, the same as GNU pr.

prs.title: pr stops merged output after the last line
prs.broken: When merging files with no page footer, pr filled the rest of the page with blank lines. Two short lines came out as 56, where GNU pr prints 2.
prs.changed: pr now stops once every file has run out, unless a footer needs the page filled.
prs.matters: Merged output is the same length as GNU pr, with no pages of blank lines.

prs.title: numfmt refuses suffixed numbers too large to print
prs.broken: In the Rust numfmt, a huge number written with a suffix, like 1Y, printed a rounded and wrong value instead of failing.
prs.changed: It now stops with the same error as GNU, and the message follows GNU's wording.
prs.matters: Scripts that convert sizes get an error, not a silently wrong number.
